title: Auditor fanout: credit-warden for non-invasive traffic duplication and tenant budgeting
creator: Lina Chen
description: Build a non-invasive "observation" fanout layer ("Auditor") that duplicates a bounded fraction of production inference requests to candidate model variants without affecting user-visible latency or reliability. The fanout must: 1) never exceed per-tenant duplicate token budgets, 2) support adaptive sampling based on tenant credits and runtime pressure, 3) provide strong tenant isolation so duplicates are cancellable and never contribute to downstream rate limits, and 4) emit accounting telemetry suitable for chargeback and automated rollback triggers.
comments: 2026-02-20 - Lina Chen: Scoped initial requirements with PM + SRE. We need a solution that avoids adding tail latency to the main request path. Proposal: sidecar-based duplication via async append-to-queue, with a separate consumer pool for auditor traffic.

2026-02-24 - Diego Morales: Spike complete. Implemented prototype sidecar that performs non-blocking duplication using a local ring buffer. Observed no p99 change in synthetic load test (within noise). Recorded duplicate_token_count metric; baseline included.

2026-02-27 - SRE Review: Raised concerns around uncontrolled burst draining from the auditor queue during downstream model restarts. Action: add 'credit-warden' that enforces a draining rate proportional to tenant credit and global budget.

2026-03-02 - Design sync (with PM Asha Patel): Agreed on tenant-weighted reservoir sampling for low-volume tenants and burst-proportional leashing for high-volume tenants. Acceptance criteria: duplicates should not cause more than 2% additional GPU utilization by default and must be abortable per-tenant.

2026-03-04 - Diego Morales: Implemented credit-warden. Key behaviors: per-tenant ledger in Redis (expiry 1h) backed by a token-bucket; adaptive sampling factor computed from remaining credits and current replica-latency pressure; fallback to 0% sampling when global duplicate budget exhausted.

2026-03-06 - QA: Ran multi-tenant replay with mixed workloads. Found an edge case where short-lived tenants with zero history were assigned high sample weights. Mitigation: initialize new tenants with conservative default credit and exponential ramp-up over first 10k tokens.

2026-03-08 - Security review note: Auditor duplicates must be redacted for PII before persistence. Added pre-write redaction hook for known fields; engineering to coordinate with Privacy for schema coverage.

2026-03-09 - Diego Morales: Added graphite/grafana dashboards and alerting rules. Metrics added: auditor.duplicate_token_count, auditor.drop_rate_by_tenant, auditor.queue_depth, auditor.replica_error_rate, auditor.duplicate_latency_p95. Dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/abcd123/auditor-duplication

2026-03-10 - Lina Chen: Linked PR and design doc: Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Auditor+Fanout+Design; PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7821. Next: canary rollout plan using dedicated small tenants and automatic rollback when replica_error_rate > 1% for 5m or duplicate_cost_overrun > 15% of budget.

2026-03-10 - Follow-ups created: (1) Add per-tenant billing-tag propagation in duplication pipeline (ENG-305679), (2) Integrate with rollout controller for automated disable of duplication when canary metrics regress (ENG-305680).
Acceptance criteria:
- Non-blocking duplication path with p99 production latency delta <= 5ms
- Per-tenant duplicate token budget enforced and observable
- Sampling adapts based on credit and global pressure; new tenants start conservatively
- Duplicates isolated from production quotas and can be killed without affecting user traffic
- Dashboards + alerts in place and team runbook updated for auto-disable and manual quarantine
QA steps:
- Run multi-tenant synthetic workload including tiny, medium, large tenants and verify duplicate_token_count respects budgets
- Trigger downstream model restart and ensure auditor queue drains at bounded rate (no surge to GPUs)
- Simulate PII payloads and verify redaction before any persisted copy
- Canary rollout: start at 0.5% global sample on 3 non-critical tenants, monitor auditor.replica_error_rate and duplicate_cost_overrun for 24h.
